subject: Tandem / what to look at first

messages.text:
Hi Luis!

When a rider calls from the street we have to talk them through which pin to pick, and half the time the bike's gone by the time they get there. So I'd like the first workshop to be about that bit, getting to a dock with a bike they can actually use. The map's a means to an end for us. It's what I liked in your Brightwell work, you started from the person standing there.

I've copied Dan because he gets the calls when this goes wrong.

Thanks, Chiara

Hi Luis

At the Ashwin Street dock on my old handset the orange pin still showed a bike after it had gone. By the time I'd put my phone away and got there I was looking at an empty slot. That's a better place to start than the colours.

Dan

Let's start at Ashwin Street and try to get to a bike with both phones. I'd take the map colours out of the first workshop. We can lay out where the info comes from in the room afterwards, once we've seen what the rider actually gets.

Thanks,
Luis

Luis Cordero
Lead Product Designer, Acme Studio
3rd floor, 48 Turnmill Street, London EC1M 5RR

Can you still hear it out loud tonight? Twenty minutes max. I've timed it and the actual speech is three if nobody laughs, which is a risk i'm willing to take lol. It's for my cousin and he is very against me doing the bit about the keys so obviously that is where we begin.

“When Rob moved out, Auntie Jean asked him to leave the keys in the blue bowl. We all know the blue bowl. I don't think he's ever finished a sentence without somebody putting a set of keys into that bowl. So he took the bowl with him. It was six weeks before he realised because he'd been keeping his own keys in his shoe.

The first time I went round to see Rob and Elise, the bowl was on the hall table. And I put my keys in it without thinking. I kept thinking about that on the way home. I think that's when I understood he'd made a home that felt like his, and that I was welcome in it.”

Then I have to stand up properly and say to Rob and Elise? Do I need to tell people to pick up thier glasses or do they just do it?

J

tell them to raise their glasses. otherwise everyone points at their glass and looks round to see what the person next to them is doing.

the bowl bit works for me but you need to get to elise a lot sooner. try the line about going round first. then jean can be annoyed about the bowl in the middle and we've met both of them before we're halfway through. i don't know what 'stand up properly' means unless you're planning to do the first part from under a table.

actually try stopping after 'welcome in it'. you had a whole extra bit about looking for somewhere to park when you told me this last week. you can just leave the room quiet for a second there.

six at mine? dentist's at 5.20 so if you get there first go and get a coffee and text me.

Six was a lie I told myself about what time I'd get out. Still on the bus lol. Could we try tomorrow? I've moved Elise up and left the shoe in for now.

J

Hamish Fairweather
